hero.lede: No invented clients, no invented numbers. These are projects I designed and built, what each one had to solve, and what it does today.
hero.note: Screenshots are from the real applications.

items.name: Car Info Lookup
items.challenge: Checking a vehicle should take seconds. Garages, buyers and parking staff had to look up plate numbers through slow, awkward channels.
items.solution: Two native apps — Swift for iOS, Java for Android — that take a licence plate, query an external vehicle data API and return make, model, year, colour, engine and inspection dates in one screen.
items.experience: One field, one button, one clear result. The interface is in Hebrew, and the app behaves the same on both platforms.
items.result: A working lookup flow on iOS and Android, suited to verification, parking and quick reference.

shots.alt: Car Info app opening screen with the garage name and logo
Car Info search screen with a plate number field and a search button
Car Info result screen listing model, manufacturer, year, colour, engine number and inspection dates

items.name: Networking — Social Platform
items.challenge: Build a complete social platform: accounts, a feed people can interact with, and messaging that arrives instantly rather than on refresh.
items.solution: A full-stack web application with secure sign-up and login, password recovery, a post feed with likes and comments, follow notifications, and direct messaging over WebSockets.
items.experience: Sign up, find people, post, follow and chat — with live notifications and a dark mode, on desktop and phone.
items.result: Deployed on Vercel with authentication, live notifications and messaging working end to end.

shots.alt: Social platform login screen with email and password fields
Social platform registration form with username, name, email and password fields

items.name: WhatsApp Automation Bot
items.challenge: Useful daily updates are only useful if they actually arrive — and nobody wants to send them by hand every morning.
items.solution: A Node.js service that pulls live weather data and a daily quote from external APIs, fills message templates and delivers them on schedule through the Twilio WhatsApp API.
items.experience: The message simply arrives on WhatsApp every day, formatted for the conditions of that morning.
items.result: Runs unattended: fetched, composed and delivered automatically, with no one in the loop.

items.name: Go Nature — Park Management
items.challenge: Park services were handled separately for staff and visitors, with no shared system behind bookings and day-to-day operations.
items.solution: A client-server Java system on a shared database, with separate interfaces for administrators and visitors and real-time communication between them.
items.experience: Staff manage orders and availability from a control application; visitors book and check in through their own flow.
items.result: A working multi-user system, built and delivered with a team of five.

principles.title: Four things that shape every project.

items.title: Start with the problem
items.text: Technology is the last decision, not the first. What's slow, manual or unclear today decides what gets built.

items.title: Build the smallest useful thing
items.text: One workflow, proven in real use, beats a year-long plan that never ships.

items.title: Connect, don't replace
items.text: Most businesses already run on tools that work. The value is usually in joining them up.

items.title: Own the result
items.text: Design, engineering, integration and launch are one job, and I stay responsible for all of it.
Back-end architecture with Node.js and Express, MySQL and MongoDB databases, integration work with front-end teams in React, and deployment with Docker.
